content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged tortoise frame. Host frame: the tortoise sets the outline, body size, and overall frame. A single creature combining a tortoise and a domestic goat. The head is that of the tortoise, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: tortoise body and legs, with its own shell over the shoulders, back, flanks, belly, and hips, and its own scaly skin on the face; from the domestic goat, as parts and materials on the tortoise's own body, dense fur in its own colors, grown from the skin as the tortoise's own covering over the crown of the head, neck, legs, and tail. This covering replaces the tortoise's scaly skin there and conforms to the tortoise's body, sized to the tortoise's body and following its contours. Every covered part keeps the tortoise's own length and shape, and the tail stays the tortoise's own tail. The scaly skin stops at the covering's edge, and the face keeps the tortoise's own scaly skin. The tortoise's shell keeps its own form and bony plates, with only its color taken from the domestic goat. The covering follows the body's own shape. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (grassland): dark back and light belly (strong countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing tortoise-goat hybrid**
I'm planning a 1:1 natural-history illustration where a tortoise sets the frame and a goat contributes fur and color, with a fully visible tortoise head, scaly face, and fur covering crown, neck, legs, and tail.
**Drafting natural history illustration**
I'm composing a side three-quarter view of the tortoise-goat hybrid with a goat-colored shell, fur on the crown, neck, legs, and tail, and hooves, set on a plain light background with natural lighting.
**Refining creature anatomy**
I'm preparing another 1:1 generation to replace the claws and scaled front legs with hooves and a more natural look, while keeping the tail and overall composition.
